name: "Freezer Friendly" Homemade Chicken Stock with Bonus Shredded Chicken (Batch-Cooking)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe makes about 16 cups (4 liters) of stock and 3 cups (1 lb) of shredded chicken. We suggest dividing stock into 4-cup portions and chicken into 1-cup portions, but you know what best suits your needs and cooking habits.
Pat chicken dry with paper towels and transfer to a large baking sheet pan. Drizzle with oil, season with salt and pepper, then toss to coat. Spread out in an even layer.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ½ lb chicken thighs, bone-in skin-on
1 ½ lb chicken drumsticks
1 tbsp neutral vegetable oil
1 tsp salt
½ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Place chicken in the oven (it doesn't have to be fully heated) and roast, turning halfway, until golden brown and cooked through, 20-25 minutes. Remove from oven.
Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 stick celery
1 small bunch Italian (flat-leaf) parsley
½ small pkg fresh thyme

instructions.primary_message: Peel carrots (if desired), then trim and roughly chop. Rougly chop celery (including any leaves). Place both in a large pot.
Roughly chop parsley (including stems). Add parsley and whole thyme sprigs to the pot with the carrot and celery.
Peel onions (if desired) and roughly chop. Add to the pot along with salt, peppercorns, and bay leaves.

When the chicken is done, transfer to the pot. Add hot water (from the tap), stir to combine, then set the pot over high heat and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce heat to medium-low and simmer, occasionally skimming away any scum from the surface with a ladle, until stock is golden in color and reduced by one-third, about 3 hours. Remove from heat. (Adjust heat, as needed, to maintain a steady, gentle simmer.)

When the stock is done simmering, remove chicken to a plate using tongs. Shred the chicken using two forks (removing the skin and bones as you go); use one fork to hold the chicken and the other fork to pull and shred the meat. Once the chicken is cool, divide between containers, cover, and refrigerate or freeze until ready to use. (Shredded chicken can be used in soups, stews, as a filling for enchiladas or quesadillas, or used in a traditional chicken salad for sandwiches.)

Pour the stock through a strainer into another large pot (or large bowl). Discard vegetable solids. Divide stock between four 4-cup containers (leaving 1-inch headroom at the top) and let cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally, about 1 hour. (Any fat will rise to the surface as the stock cools.)
Once the stock has cooled to room temperature, carefully skim away any fat from the surface.

STORING: Cover each container with an air-tight lid (or wrap tightly with plastic wrap). Place in the freezer for up to 6 months. HEATING: For best results, thaw stock in the fridge overnight before using. You can also add frozen stock to simmering soups, sauces, or stews, stirring until fully melted.
